problem: Indoor mobile robot navigation needs robust general object recognition; the standard BoW model discards spatial relationships between feature points, and specifying goals in unknown, dynamic environments is inconvenient.
motivation: Object recognition is the basis for semantic navigation in indoor scenes. Adding spatial layout information to BoW features should improve recognition, and a hand-drawn semantic map offers a simple human-robot interface for unknown and dynamic environments.
key_idea: Extend BoW feature vectors with statistics of relative distances and angles between SIFT feature points (GPU-accelerated), classify objects with an SVM, and navigate using a hand-drawn semantic map for human-robot interaction.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The claim is that adding spatial-relationship statistics to BoW adds useful redundant information and improves recognition robustness.
method: Extended BoW: augments standard BoW histograms with statistical spatial-relationship information (relative distances and angles) of all feature points in an image.
GPU-accelerated SIFT: detects and describes local features quickly for the BoW model.
SVM classifier: classifies objects from the extended BoW feature vectors.
Hand-drawn semantic map HRI: the user sketches a semantic map to guide the robot in unknown and dynamic indoor environments.

setting.training_data: not stated in abstract (object image dataset for SVM)
setting.action_space: not specified (mobile robot navigation to recognized objects/landmarks)

results: The abstract claims the navigation technology is very robust and highly effective, without any quantitative numbers or baselines.
limitations: Only qualitative claims; no quantitative results or benchmarks in the abstract
Relies on hand-crafted SIFT/BoW/SVM pipeline and user-drawn maps
